name: Lennon Sanders
life: “I still remember breakfast after a child's first early sailing lesson.” On Tuesday, near Breakwater Way, Lennon stops on the landward side of the cycle track to watch the first boats turn for home.
voice: I teach their son. His favorite part of Sunday is actually the walk to breakfast afterward.
appearance: Lennon is easy to recognize by a center part and straight chestnut hair and fine brows over wide-set eyes. Usually dressed in a faded indigo overshirt with a seam let out by a narrow strip of contrasting fabric, Lennon folds a paper napkin into quarters without noticing when listening.
personality: Lennon feels a room through sound. A door slammed in high spirits can produce the same instant startle as an angry one, and it takes a little while to hear what actually follows.
agenda: To keep the breakfast ritual the son really likes.
family: Marlowe Paige is Lennon’s half-sibling. Lennon chooses whether they walk home or sit a while. Marlowe brings a spare shopping bag. That small arrangement gives both a reason to see each other on weeks when asking for company outright feels difficult. Asked about *The broken till*, Marlowe says, “I put down too much money to avoid looking broke.”
connections: Alfred Ross. The teacher and new partner have reasons to preserve a morning at the breakfast table ashore.

reactions.situation: A child wants both separated adults on the same boat
reactions.response: Lennon asks each adult whether sharing one trip is possible without putting the child in the middle.
